intro: Mosaics are waiting for you at the Hatay Archaeology Museum, in Hatay province, founded in 1948. It holds one of the richest mosaic collections in the world, lifted from the Roman villas of Antioch and Samandağ.
history: Antioch was the third city of the Roman Empire, and in the villas around it floor mosaics were laid on an extraordinary scale. A museum was founded in 1948 for what the excavations of the 1930s had brought to light, and in 2014 the collection moved to a new building. Look closely as you go: these mosaics show not only mythological scenes but daily life, dining tables and charms against the evil eye.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Oceanus and Tethys mosaic and 'The Black-Eyed Woman', then the Yakto mosaic, the Hittite lion and the Antioch sarcophagi.
facts: Did you know? The museum's 'Evil Eye' mosaic paints the curse as an eye and sets crows, a scorpion and a snake upon it: a charm against bad luck from the second century AD. And remember the city behind it all. Antioch was the third city of the Roman Empire, and the floors of the villas around it make up one of the richest collections of Roman mosaic in the world.
outro: This brings our tour of the Hatay Archaeology Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These floors were walked on by the people of Antioch; now they are ours to protect. Enjoy your visit.
